lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: describing a concern accurately to a professional

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic describing a concern accurately to a professional task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Read this fictional situation: Rowan has had a mild headache on and off for the past four days.
safetyNotes: The learner works entirely from the provided fictional scenario about Rowan; no real concern, symptom, or health detail of the learner's own is required or requested anywhere in this lesson.
If a learner has a real concern they want to discuss, they should raise it separately with a trusted adult -- it does not belong in this assignment.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Compare your description from task 2 to a vague version like 'I have a headache.' What specifically would a professional be able to do with your version that they couldn't do with the vague one?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Timeframe specificity: Names the specific timeframe given in the scenario (four days). | Follow-up answer completeness: Answers both follow-up questions using specific details drawn from the scenario. | Precision reflection: Names one specific thing a professional could do with the precise version that they couldn't with the vague one. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner rewrite the same description as if explaining it to a friend instead of a professional, then write one sentence identifying what changed in the wording and why that change was necessary.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: describing a concern accurately to a professional coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Read this fictional situation: Rowan has had a mild headache on and off for the past four days.
Coach direction: Before drafting, think about why vague descriptions slow a professional down.

Learner prompt: Think of a time you (or someone you know) said something like 'I just don't feel good' to describe a problem. What information was missing that would have helped someone else understand it faster?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: describing a concern accurately to a professional complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using the fictional scenario provided, write the specific opening description you would give.

Response 1 (t2-p1): Using only the fictional scenario given (Rowan's headache), write the exact sentence or two you would say to describe the concern, including when it started and how it has changed since then.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My description states a specific timeframe (when it started, how long) rather than a vague word like 'a while' or 'lately.'
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: describing a concern accurately to a professional minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Compare your description from task 2 to a vague version like 'I have a headache.' What specifically would a professional be able to do with your version that they couldn't do with the vague one?

Success checks: Timeframe specificity: Names the specific timeframe given in the scenario (four days). | Follow-up answer completeness: Answers both follow-up questions using specific details drawn from the scenario. | Precision reflection: Names one specific thing a professional could do with the precise version that they couldn't with the vague one.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: describing a concern accurately to a professional supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional describing a concern accurately to a professional condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Timeframe specificity: Names the specific timeframe given in the scenario (four days). | Follow-up answer completeness: Answers both follow-up questions using specific details drawn from the scenario. | Precision reflection: Names one specific thing a professional could do with the precise version that they couldn't with the vague one..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
